chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no [valid] emancipation except what is sought by it the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a formulaic divine epithet used after the name of Allah
key_terms.عِتْق: Emancipation, manumission — the Islamic legal act of freeing a slave
key_terms.وَجْهُ اللَّهِ: The Face of Allah — a Quranic expression denoting seeking God's pleasure and approval, not mere appearance

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for valid emancipation of slaves in Shia Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the theological and legal condition for a valid emancipation of slaves: the act must be done purely for the sake of seeking the pleasure of Allah, not for worldly motives. This ruling situates the freeing of slaves within the Islamic framework of sincere intention (niyyah) and divine-oriented action. In the context of seventh-century Islamic jurisprudence, when slavery was a social institution, this hadith placed strict conditions on the legal act of manumission, ensuring it retained its spiritual dimension as an act of worship.
